steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper baking cups.
Stir together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Whisk together milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla in a separate bowl until evenly blended; set aside.

Beat sugar and butter with an electric mixer in a large bowl until light and fluffy. The mixture should be noticeably lighter in color. Add eggs one at a time, allowing each egg to blend into the butter mixture before adding the next. Pour in the flour mixture alternately with the milk mixture, mixing until just incorporated.

Divide cake batter into four separate bowls. Add a few drops of food coloring into one bowl of batter and stir; add more food coloring if necessary to reach the desired shade. Repeat with remaining colors and bowls of batter.
Using a different spoon for each color batter, spoon a small portion of each color into the cupcake liners, until 1/2 to 3/4 full. Do not mix the batter once it is in the cupcake liner.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into a cupcake comes clean, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Rainbow Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: Learn how to make rainbow cupcakes here. Vanilla cake batter is mixed with food coloring and layered to make cute treats that will delight all ages!

review.reviewBody: I have made this various times and I love it!!!!! Especially when you take it out of the wrapper and cut it in half to see all the pretty layers!!!! I would definently want all of you to try it!

I had a week's notice to make these for an activity on the following weekend and so I did a "test run" of this recipe every day. Each day I modified something. What I found is that on batch #1, adding 1/2 cup sour cream creates a more moist cupcake; however, it's a little more "dense." For batch #2, I didn't put any sour cream, but instead put 1/2 cup applesauce. This gave a more "fluffy" texture. Finally, for batch #3, I made no modifications, immediately covered the cupcakes with cling wrap and let them sit for one day. This too moistened them. Ultimately, I chose the applesauce method and combined it with the "sit for one day" method. It was what my particular gang preferred; however, I can see why other people would prefer the moistness offered by the sour cream method.

Sift your flour! After reading so many reviews mentioning these were dry, I guessed that people were putting in too much flour. Scoop and level compacts the flour and you can get too much. We sifted ours, spooned into the cup, then leveled. Cakes in particular are very sensitive to the right amount of flour. Ours turned out tender and moist. The colors were beautiful (we used paste colors, which are more vibrant than liquid). Perfect for my daughter's painting themed birthday party!

I made these for my sisters class tomorrow and they turned out great.I haven't actually tried them yet, but they cooked, look, and smell amazing! I didn't color them, i was only looking for a vanilla cupcake recipe. People were saying that they were dry, so I only did 2 1/4 cup flour. I also added 2 tsp. vanilla and did half whole wheat flour. I also cooked at 325 degrees and baked them for about 22 minutes. Definitely a keeper. Thanks :) (Though i did only get 21 cupcakes from them, but that's okay because she only needed 19.)

an important part of the recipe is that you use SOFTENED BUTTER instead of melted butter. it creates that lighter color mentioned in the directions and when it comes out of the oven it makes the cake softer. i have made this twice both ways and when i made this with melted butter the cake was dry and crumbly so i switched to softened butter and it was so much better.

The first time i did a these cupcakes they were okay but VERY dry. I then gave them another dry but changed it up a little. Since i dont have any eggs at room temperature i put some eggs in a glass full of warm water, i then softened the butter for about 10 sec. and i Folded in 1/2 cup sour cream to the prepared batter they turned out great, they were deffinetly not dry anymore.

I made these for my son's class on his birthday. They were a big hit. I did find the batter very thick after adding the food colouring. It was difficult to spoon into the cups so I ended up piping it and then had to smooth it out each layer with a wet spoon. This recipe is time consuming but the effect is great. I was able to squeeze 26 cupcakes out of the batter. I would suggest using paste type colouring as the liquid stuff does not give the brightest colours.
Exchanged white sugar with brown and mixed in some whole wheat flour. Kids loved it.

Great recipe! I did make a few tweaks. I always bake with corn oil instead of vegetable oil and use a lower temperature and have never had an issue cakes being dry. I also used a touch more vanilla and less flour. I didn't have red food dye, so I threw in pinch of cherry jello mix. They looked and tasted great! Definitely will make again!

After following a reviewers suggestion to substitute applesauce for butter, that is the only change I made. The batter was more dense than a box version but I’m guessing that’s because the colored layers need to hold up. After baking them and letting them cool, the cupcake was more solid than light, like I’m use to eating. The flavor was good but not worth the effort unfortunately. The presentation was beautiful spin cutting, thanks.

I have used many different cake/cupcake recipes, at first I was concerned with the amount of egg in the recipe but the cupcakes turned out amazing! I took them to another level by stuffing a Girl Guide cookie in the Middle. I recommend this recipe 100%
They kind of taste like cornbread, and a lot of my friend who ate them thought that too.
Thanks turned out great
DELICOUS GREAT AMAing cupcakes

These were delicious and turned out so cute! We followed the recipe exactly and made two batches of 17 cupcakes (didn't quite make it to 24). My only complaint is that the recipe uses a ton of bowls, 3 for the batter + 1 bowl for each color. We did 5 colors and I used a finger dipped in water to spread out the layers to the edges of the cupcake liner. It was more time intensive but made for a better reveal when bit into. They were not dry at all. Our bake time was 15 minutes for the first batch and 17 minutes for the second (they were slightly more full). The cake had a fluffy crumb, they rose well (slightly rounded tops), and a sweet buttery flavor. I love that the recipe used 1/2 oil (for use and less expensive!) and 1/2 butter (for the flavor!).
Everyone at the party thought that they were good. I thought that they were a little dry. I will add some almond paste to the recipe and some orange zest.
